hevc.fact: HEVC is H.265, first published in 2013; profiles vary.
VLC documents raw-HEVC and HEVC decoding; official release text inspected and saved as scratch/vlc3.txt.

ico.fact: Icons can contain differently sized images and mask or graded transparency.

m2ts.fact: M2TS adds four bytes to 188-byte transport packets and may carry several stream types.

mkv.fact: Matroska organizes multimedia tracks and related elements.

mov.fact: MOV/QuickTime packaging is separate from encoded tracks; normal unfragmented files need complete metadata.
QuickTime wraps various media and uses atom-based structures; video/quicktime identifies movies.

mpeg.fact: MPEG-1/MPEG-2 program-stream writers are distinct from MPEG-4-family containers.

mpg.fact: FFmpeg MPEG program-stream output uses the MPEG container family rather than a distinct MPG codec.

mp4.fact: MP4 Part14 was standardized in 2003 and is an ISO base media subtype.

aac.fact: Standalone AAC can use ADTS; registered audio/aac also covers LATM/LOAS.

swf.fact: SWF authoring can embed FLV or load external video; embedded H264 guides differ.
Adobe Flash Player reached end of life and blocks content.

otf.fact: OpenType was jointly developed by Microsoft and Adobe and supports advanced typography.

svg.fact: SVG drawing may contain paths or embedded raster content.

png.fact: PNG has different color types and sample depths and uses lossless storage.

hdr.fact: Greg Ward invented RGBE; three color bytes share an exponent.
The Radiance registered image type is image/vnd.radiance.

ppm.fact: P6 binary and P3 plain forms differ; maximum values can reach65535 and image sequences are allowed.

jpg.fact: JPEG output is lossy even at high quality settings.
